extracted.intended_audience: marketing, advertising, media, PR and communications professionals (entrants and jurors) preparing or judging Mumbrella Awards 2026 entries
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and judging rules for submitting and evaluating entries to the 2026 Mumbrella Awards across campaign, craft, agency/team and culture categories, including live judging requirements and category-specific scoring notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging criteria — idea, execution and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: the judging criteria has been streamlined, with most categories now weighted across idea, execution and effectiveness to emphasise measurable impact alongside creative quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most categories use a three-part weighting (idea; execution; effectiveness). Entrants should therefore present a clear creative idea, high-quality executional detail, and measurable evidence of impact. Scoring favours entries that balance creative quality with demonstrable, measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft — executional excellence
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft & Craft-related categories are judged primarily on executional/technical quality (film/motion craft, design/visual craft, digital & UX craft etc.) rather than effectiveness or broad strategic metrics. Provide detail on craft choices, techniques and executional complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency, leadership and culture awards — broader criteria (sustained performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: agency, leadership and culture awards retain broader criteria to recognise sustained performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories assess longer-term contribution and sustained performance across an agency/team/leader/culture — not just a single campaign. Entrants should include evidence of ongoing results, organisational culture, leadership impact and sustained business/brand outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition — creative, commercial, cultural and strategic standing
rubrics_metrics.description: The ambition is simple: to recognise work that not only stands out creatively, but stands up commercially, culturally and strategically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries should demonstrate multiple dimensions: standout creative idea, commercial/financial impact, cultural resonance and strategic clarity. Evidence and metrics supporting commercial and cultural impact strengthen effectiveness scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury mindset — reward catalysts and risk-taking
rubrics_metrics.description: Reward the work everyone agrees on — the polished, the box-ticking. Or back the Catalyst. The work that moved first, took chances, made us uncomfortable. Catalysts carry the risk. I hope you’ll have their back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges are explicitly encouraged to value bold, pioneering work ('Catalysts') that took risks and shifted thinking, not just safe polished entries. Entrants should highlight originality, first-mover advantage and the risks they took and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist & live judging day — presentation and pitch requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Should you qualify in the preliminary round of judging and make the coveted shortlist, you will take part in the live judging day ... present and pitch just what sets your entry apart from the competition. Convince the judges and you could end up seeing your name up in lights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shortlisted entrants must prepare a live presentation/pitch for the live judging day (Hilton Sydney, 21 May 2026). The live pitch is a material part of final evaluation — entrants should craft succinct, persuasive live presentations and be ready for Q&A/face-to-face scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industry Leader of the Year — live component at Mumbrella360
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction of a live component for Industry Leader of the Year at Mumbrella360 further reinforces transparency, credibility and community engagement, while keeping the majority of scoring firmly in the hands of our expert jurors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry Leader assessment now includes an in-person/live element in addition to juror scoring. While live performance and community engagement matter, the majority of the final score still comes from jurors' evaluations. Prepare both submission materials and any live presentation elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holdco of the Year — aggregate score only
rubrics_metrics.description: Holdco of the Year - AGGREGATE SCORE ONLY
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holdco of the Year is judged via an aggregate scoring mechanism (not an open-entry single submission). Expect evaluation based on aggregated metrics/scores across constituent agencies/brands; provide information that will contribute to aggregate calculations where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency of the Year — nominated only
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency of the Year - NOMINATED ONLY
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency of the Year is not an open entry category; agencies must be nominated. Nomination-only status changes submission expectations — judges will assess nominated agencies on the provided nomination material and sustained performance evidence rather than standalone campaign entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigour & process — preliminary round, shortlist, live judging
rubrics_metrics.description: At Mumbrella, we want to ensure these awards remain the most rigorous in town. Should you qualify in the preliminary round of judging and make the coveted shortlist, you will take part in the live judging day ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards use a staged evaluation: preliminary round (paper/entry assessment), shortlist announcement, then live judging for shortlisted entries. Entrants should structure submissions to succeed in written review and to support a compelling live pitch if shortlisted.
